extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and policymakers interested in Korean War and U.S. domestic policy
extracted.subtask_short: Korean War and US policy reporting
extracted.subtask_description: A contemporary newspaper report covering developments in the Korean War, U.S. defense and mobilization measures, domestic economic proposals (taxes/controls), agricultural supply assessments, and related government actions. Summaries of executive orders, congressional activity, and military judgments are presented for a general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screen all civil public works for postponement/curtailment
rubrics_metrics.description: "Screening all civil public works with the purpose of postponing/curtailing..." (part of the President's order to federal agencies to lower demand on resources needed for defense).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is listed as the first numbered directive in President Truman's order: federal programs should be reexamined with particular attention to screening civil public works so they can be postponed or curtailed where appropriate to reduce civilian competition for services, commodities, raw materials, manpower and facilities needed for defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tighten credit programs except those directly contributing to defense/international responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: "Tightening all credit programs except those directly contributing to meeting these defense and international responsibilities."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second numbered directive of the presidential order: federal credit programs are to be tightened (i.e., more restrictive) unless the credit directly supports defense or obligations related to international responsibilities. Implied scoring/exception rule: maintain credit for defense-related programs, restrict others to lower demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold purchases of supplies and equipment to a minimum; cut stocks; turn surplus over to GSA
rubrics_metrics.description: "Holding the purchase of supplies and equipment to a minimum, especially those of cars, typewriters and other equipments using critical materials. The President said stocks should be cut to lowest practical levels and surplus supplies and equipment should be turned over immediately to the General Services Administration."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third numbered directive: agencies should minimize nonessential procurement, prioritize reduction of inventories to the lowest practical level, and immediately reallocate surplus items to the GSA for potential reassignment to defense needs. Examples called out: cars, typewriters and other items using critical materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senate authorization to regulate operation of foreign ships in American waters
rubrics_metrics.description: Senate voted to give authority to guard and control operation of all foreign ships in American waters; text notes "regulation of the movement of foreign ships, and carries penalties of 10 years imprisonment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale included that customs inspection alone is insufficient; authority would enable regulation of foreign-flag movements and anchorage and impose criminal penalties (up to 10 years) for violations. This is presented as a legal/regulatory measure to protect against the use of foreign tramp ships to cause hazards (e.g., atomic disasters) or other security risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed immediate across-the-board tax increases and excess-profits measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal by the Senate-House Economic Committee for an immediate multi‑billion dollar 'across the board' boost in federal taxes to crack down on profiteers and fund the Korean crisis; discussion includes raising individual taxes 10% and restoring an 85% wartime excess-profits tax (with debate over applying to this year's income vs. next year's).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance/context: committee leaders thought a substantial tax increase was needed; some favored applying increases to the current year's income (including a 10% individual tax boost and excess-profits taxation) while others opposed retroactive measures and preferred making increases effective in the following tax year. The entry frames political and practical considerations (retroactivity, base for excess-profit calculations, likely timing of congressional action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Army call-up policy for National Guard and Reserves (progressive, non-divisional, 30-day notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Department of the Army is in the process of progressively calling non-divisional elements of both National Guard and Reserves to active duty as the need arises and facilities for their reception and training can be provided... Units will be alerted approximately 30 days prior to movement... For the immediate present it is not contemplated that units the size of a division will be called."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational criteria: call-ups focus on non-divisional/combat support units (field artillery, armored cavalry, engineers, quartermaster outfits, signal corps, military police, transportation units); calls are made in smaller-than-division groupings, with ~30 days' notice to permit personal arrangements; voluntary active service requests are solicited (individuals given up to 30 days to report). This defines the procedural standard for mobilization in the reported plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military criteria limiting practical use of the atomic bomb in Korea
rubrics_metrics.description: Military officials questioned whether the A-bomb could produce results in Korea, noting that to be "profitable" its use would require thousands or tens of thousands of troops concentrated in an area a mile or less in radius, that Korea's mountainous terrain and dispersed enemy dispositions reduce effectiveness, and that the U.S. arsenal is necessarily limited in size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance/justification from the article: effective A-bomb use requires dense troop concentrations or strategic industrial targets; the terrain and lack of concentrated targets in North Korea make it impractical; logistical and material costs and limited stockpiles of bombs weigh heavily in decisions. The entry summarizes the strategic criteria and constraints the armed forces apply when judging feasibility of using atomic weapons.

rubrics_metrics.name: UN handling of offers for troops — official government offers only; UN not recruiting volunteer international ground force
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary‑General Trygve Lie and his office made clear the UN is not recruiting a secret international ground force and that offers of elements for service must come from governments — individuals wishing to volunteer must deal with their own governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy/procedural standard: in response to offers of planes, ships, hospital supplies and individual volunteers, Lie's stance is that any contribution of forces or elements must be governmental and handled through official channels; the UN will not accept or process individual volunteers directly. The article notes replies from member governments are being awaited and that offers must be handled formally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agriculture Department food-supply assessment standards and measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agriculture Department report (expected) will present statistical information on major food items, concluding there is no valid reason to fear food shortages; notes include that wheat for flour and bakery products is 30–40% above anticipated market demand, milk production is near record levels (with part diverted to government surplus stocks), butter surpluses exceed 185,000,000 pounds, and world sugar production is at a record requiring import restrictions to protect domestic prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entry captures the quantitative metrics and policy responses cited: comparing current stocks/production to anticipated demand (e.g., percent-above demand for wheat), tracking production trends (milk, eggs, fruits, vegetables), and the use of import restrictions to prevent foreign supplies from depressing domestic prices. It also notes expected price effects for certain items (fruits, lard/vegetable oils) and the implication for supply management and government support programs.
